Nandini ghee's pricing varies significantly based on the packaging, including a notable increase for certain sizes. In addition, the cost of butter and paneer has also been updated in this revision.

items.title: Inside the chip talent war: Trade secrets and rising Chinese rivals
items.summary: Growing competition for semiconductor talent is fueling a battle over trade secrets as Chinese chipmakers gain ground.

items.title: EAM Jaishankar discusses economic partnership, CETA with UK’s Burnham on CHOGM sidelines
items.summary: S Jaishankar met UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham in Antigua and Barbuda for CHOGM 2026 discussions. They focused on strengthening economic partnerships under the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement. Jaishankar emphasized the importance of digital solutions and climate initiatives during a Commonwealth meeting. He highlighted local distribution networks and the role of the Indian business community in fostering connections.

items.title: US sanctions India-based couple, companies over alleged support for Iran's Shadow oil fleet
items.summary: The United States imposed sanctions on Suniel Kumar Sharma and Jaspreet Preeti Shahid for aiding Iran's shadow fleet. Their network allegedly provided fraudulent maritime registrations to help sanctioned vessels transport Iranian petroleum. Several companies linked to the couple also received sanctions under Executive Order 13902. Additionally, a Turkiye-based company was sanctioned for providing services to US-designated Iranian airlines.

items.title: Australia's oldest department store David Jones folds after 188 years
items.summary: The brand's 38 physical stores and online site will continue to operate while receivers review its operations.

items.title: Snack makers tweak trade margins, engineer pouches to break ₹5 pack habit
items.summary: Rising costs of potatoes, edible oil and packaging are squeezing margins on entry-level packs, prompting snack makers to push larger SKUs, rethink packaging and expand premium offerings.

items.title: Inside India newsletter: India weighs a tax cut to win over foreign investors. Will it work?
items.summary: Foreign investors are losing their appetite for Indian equities, with their holdings touching an all-time low of 14%.

items.title: Big FMCG companies outgrow market as smaller rivals get squeezed by costs and slowing rural demand
items.summary: India's fast-moving consumer goods sector has experienced a slowdown in volume growth amid rising costs. Rural demand has weakened, impacting smaller regional manufacturers while larger companies thrive. Hindustan Unilever, Marico, and other major firms reported robust growth figures. Smaller players are particularly vulnerable due to their limited capacity to manage current challenges.

items.title: A 'demand decade' ahead for energy? BP, Baker Hughes CEOs weigh the investment outlook
items.summary: Rising energy demand offers investment opportunities, but geopolitical risks and oil price uncertainty cloud the outlook, executives and an analyst said.

items.title: Elon Musk's millions failed to deliver Republican wins in fierce midterms
items.summary: Musk spent nearly $500m in the 2026 US midterm elections, an individual election spending record.

items.title: India proposes 1% mandatory blending of green jet fuel from January
items.summary: India has introduced a draft policy for the mandatory blending of sustainable aviation fuel for international flights. The initial blending requirement is set at 1%, increasing to 5% by 2030, and 20% by 2040. Airlines must source approximately 90% of their aviation turbine fuel from international airports to curb economic tankering. Non-compliance may lead to penalties for airlines and oil marketing companies in this proposal.

items.title: Govt plans instant ban on manufacturing of drugs failing key quality tests
items.summary: Pharma companies could have their drug licenses suspended immediately if quality tests indicate failure. The health ministry's proposed changes aim to protect public health by enforcing swift action on substandard medications. Regulators would take action upon receiving a government analyst's report declaring a drug not of standard quality. Manufacturers would need to perform a root cause analysis and implement corrective actions to lift the suspension.

items.title: Kellogg's admits snap, crackle and pop is quieter after uproar over Rice Krispies recipe change
items.summary: The cereal giant has changed the recipes for Rice Krispies and Coco Pops, sparking a backlash online.

items.title: MIAL seeks to shift 14 international flights to Navi Mumbai Airport by Nov 3
items.summary: Mumbai International Airport has proposed shifting flights to 14 international destinations to the new Navi Mumbai International Airport. This move aims to free up capacity for the redevelopment of Terminal 1 at the current airport. If airlines do not voluntarily surrender slots, the airport operator plans to execute the transition. Passengers flying to Gulf and Asian destinations may have to use the new airport instead.

items.title: Mercedes plans bigger India play with greater localisation of parts
items.summary: Mercedes-Benz plans to increase its local manufacturing efforts while expanding its supplier base in India. The luxury carmaker expects to achieve record annual sales if the current trend continues. Ola Kallenius, the global chairman, highlighted the potential for Indian suppliers to support global operations. The company has committed an additional investment of ₹200 crore, raising total investments to ₹3,200 crore.

items.title: Big factories dominate India's manufacturing output, Annual Survey of Industries shows
items.summary: India's manufacturing sector is characterised by a significant concentration in large factories generating substantial output. Factories producing over ₹500 crore contribute to more than three-fifths of total value added. Smaller factories represent a large number but have minimal output and value contribution.

items.title: Battery component makers may get up to 50% capital subsidy
items.summary: The ministry of heavy industries is evaluating various subsidy models to enhance domestic battery component manufacturing capacity. Proposed support includes capital subsidies and sales-linked incentives to promote local production. India aims for sufficient manufacturing capacity to support 50 GWh of annual battery cell production by 2032. Current costs of battery materials are significantly higher compared to those from China.

items.title: New orders & robust demand lift India's October services growth to 4-month high
items.summary: Growth in India's services sector increased to a four-month high in October due to strong domestic demand and business orders. The HSBC Services Business Activity Index rose to 55.8, reflecting improved business conditions. Conversely, manufacturing activity showed a slight decline, easing to a PMI of 54.7. While input prices continued to rise, the rate of increase was the slowest in over six years.

items.title: US slaps sanctions on Indian, Turkish firms and people for aiding Iran
items.summary: The sanctions are part of the Trump administration's "Operation Economic Outcast," which aims to cut off Iran's ability to sell oil to fund the war with the US and Israel. Treasury unveiled the new sanctions a day after Democrats made huge gains in midterm elections, winning control of both houses of Congress as voters expressed anger about the Iran war and its impact in fueling US inflation.

items.title: Trump's midterm setback may give India an edge in trade deal
items.summary: US has sought to allay concerns that the Republicans’ midterm election defeat could derail trade talks with India, with an American embassy spokesperson saying that President Donald Trump remains firmly in charge of Washington’s trade agenda

items.title: Explained: Why could a weak monsoon derail India's ambitious ethanol blending programme?
items.summary: India’s weak monsoon and rising food prices are putting food security ahead of ethanol production, potentially pushing the country’s fuel-blending rate below its 20% target and increasing reliance on imported crude.

items.title: Over half of street vendors may cut UPI acceptance if 0.4% MDR is introduced: ISB study
items.summary: More than 67% of street vendors in India currently accept UPI payments for transactions. A proposed 0.4% merchant discount rate could lead to reduced acceptance among vendors. Concerns arise particularly for vendor-supplier transactions, as many vendors make payments above ₹2,000. A significant portion of vendors faced additional charges from suppliers and might pass costs onto customers.

items.title: Government prepares draft sustainable aviation fuels policy; moots mandatory blending in ATF from 2027
items.summary: The civil aviation ministry has circulated the draft National Policy on Sustainable Aviation Fuels which mandates use of only indigenously manufactured SAF to be blended with Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF).

items.title: LTCG tax relief on cards? FM acknowledges FPI concerns as SEBI, FICCI push for reforms in Budget 2027
items.summary: FM Nirmala Sitharaman said the government recognizes investor concerns about India’s investment climate and will consider feedback as it seeks to sustain growth near 7%. She acknowledged rising foreign investment outflows.

items.title: Piyush Goyal sets March 2027 deadline for digitisation of DGFT services, aims to end physical visits
items.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has set March 31, 2027, as the deadline for complete digitisation of DGFT services, including licence, permit and SCOMET approvals. From April 1, businesses will no longer need physical visits to government offices for these services. The move also includes digitising historical records and simplifying procedures.

items.title: India sees some trade relief, new risks after US midterm vote
items.summary: A bruised Trump after US midterm election results gives New Delhi some breathing room in negotiations over an India-US trade deal, reducing pressure to agree to terms it sees as unfavourable.

items.title: US midterm election results 2026: India sees some trade relief, new risks after US midterm vote
items.summary: Indian officials are cautiously optimistic about the recent US midterm election results and their implications. While the election reduces trade tension, it introduces new uncertainties for US-India relations. Analysts suggest it is too early to gauge the long-term effects of these political changes. The potential for increased tariffs still looms due to ongoing investigations.

items.title: Services sector growth hits a four-month peak in October, PMI survey shows
items.summary: Driven by strong domestic demand, HSBC's India Services PMI rose to 55.8 in October as cost pressures eased to a six-year low, even as export orders and hiring slowed.
